changes: Required View aliases are established before optional destructive alias selection; all readers and published Views contribute to shared storage liveness.
Optional writes require every actual reader to happen-before the write, using the existing bounded segment clocks. Cold reader lists retain future output readers after union.
Producer-first workspace request roots reuse the parent root in linear time.
Vulkan paged seal releases its completed internal result owner before the original native reuse gate. External GraphOutput and escaped native owners remain protected.

checks.original_numeric_controls: Both defects reproduced: {3,5} instead of {1,1}; published private View {2,3} instead of {-2,-3}.
checks.intermediate_group_only_control: 3/4 PASS; real two-context/two-lane compiled plan still selected a destructive alias despite an unordered earlier reader. Test verifies actual segment ancestors and physical alias, without relying on a probabilistic race.
checks.final_alias_and_cold_controls: 8/8 PASS: four alias tests plus four existing route retry, budget and exhaustive allocation-failure rollback controls.
checks.same_lane_reuse: The ordinary in-place chain retains its single 16-byte workspace payload.
checks.original_vulkan_page: Existing strict submit passed; added unchanged prepare_replay reproduced result-is-still-retained rejection.
checks.combined_final: Fresh common Graph core and final page owner/test linked together; same public Graph passes CPU/Vulkan Q18/Q2/Q0, two slots, retained output rejection and explicit replay after release, original FP64 tolerance 0.002.
checks.build: Related strict /W4 /WX host TUs only; existing SDK, native math, shaders and other object closure reused.

limits: No new full-model numerical acceptance or fair tokens/s comparison.
No new Apple/Linux runtime validation in this round.
Cold alias group/read-list metadata has a real memory cost; no new warm analysis or Plan/Invocation ABI fields. Compile latency and throughput were not measured.
Cross-lane regression proves the compiled dependency/alias contract; it does not claim a measured concurrent hardware race.
Vulkan ordinary dense BF16 SDPA already has a widening route. Typed BF16 paged/ragged/compact MLA wiring is only investigated and documented in this archive, not implemented here.
Immutable input-source preparation scratch still has an observed repeated allocation opportunity; unchanged here.
goal: active; broader architecture, model coverage, numerical acceptance and performance work remains
